chunks: He said: Ja'far ibn Sama'a narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan from his father, al-Hasan ibn Harun, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said:

This son of mine, that is Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), is the Qaim (the Awaited One), and he is of the inevitable [matter], and he is the one who will fill it with equity and justice, just as it was filled with tyranny and oppression.

key_terms.الْقَائِمُ: The Qaim (the Awakened One), a title for the Mahdi indicating his rising to establish justice
key_terms.الْمَحْتُومُ: The inevitable/decided one, referring to the certainty of his appearance
key_terms.جَوْرًا: Tyranny/oppression, the state of injustice from which the Qaim will deliver the world
key_terms.قِسْطًا: Equity/fairness, often used in contrast to justice in a broader sense

ai.seo_question: Who is the Qaim that will fill the earth with justice according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Kitab al-Ghayba* highlights the eschatological role of Imam al-Hadi (a.s.) as the 'Qaim' who restores divine justice, a concept central to Shia belief in the Mahdi's eventual reappearance. The phrase 'from the inevitable' (min al-mahmud) underscores the certainty of his leadership, linking the Imamate to the cosmic order of filling the earth with equity after it is saturated with tyranny.
